recognize_zh: 抹片中大量異常前骨髓球，細胞質充滿紫紅色粗大顆粒、核呈折疊或雙葉狀；放大圖（B）可見一條細長的 Auer 小體橫跨在細胞核上方（箭頭），配合牙齦出血，指向急性前骨髓球性白血病（APL）。
features: Numerous large abnormal promyelocytes with moderate N:C ratio
Folded, reniform or bilobed nuclei with fine chromatin and occasional nucleoli
Cytoplasm densely packed with coarse purple-red azurophilic granules, some obscuring the nucleus
Slender Auer rod overlying the nucleus in the highlighted cell (arrow, panel B)
Relative absence of maturing neutrophils; red cells without significant fragmentation in this field
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate/peripheral blood smear shows a predominance of large abnormal promyelocytes with folded to bilobed nuclei and abundant cytoplasm packed with coarse azurophilic granules. Normal maturing granulocytes are sparse. At high magnification, a slender Auer rod is seen superimposed over the nucleus of one cell. Findings are consistent with acute promyelocytic leukemia (hypergranular type); urgent confirmation of PML::RARA and coagulation studies for DIC are indicated.

ddx.vs: AML with maturation has blasts with a single long Auer rod and salmon perinuclear hof plus maturing granulocytes, rather than sheets of hypergranular promyelocytes with folded nuclei.

ddx.dx: Reactive promyelocyte-rich marrow (G-CSF effect or marrow recovery)
ddx.vs: Recovering marrow shows normal promyelocytes with a Golgi zone and orderly maturation, without Auer rods or bilobed nuclei.
Monocytic blasts have fine granules, gray-blue cytoplasm and are nonspecific esterase positive, while APL cells show intense MPO positivity and coarse granules.
The microgranular variant has bilobed nuclei with sparse or invisible granules, unlike the heavily granulated cells seen here.
